question:
A 30-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of the sudden onset of back pain beginning 2 hours ago. Beginning yesterday, he noticed that his eyes started appearing yellowish and his urine was darker than normal. Two months ago, he returned from a trip to Greece, where he lived before immigrating to the US 10 years ago. Three days ago, he was diagnosed with latent tuberculosis and started on isoniazid. He has worked as a plumber the last 5 years. His temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows back tenderness and scleral icterus. Laboratory studies show:
Hematocrit 29%
Leukocyte count 8000/mm3
Platelet count 280,000/mm3
Serum
Bilirubin
Total 4 mg/dL
Direct 0.7 mg/dL
Haptoglobin 15 mg/dL (N=41–165 mg/dL)
Lactate dehydrogenase 180 U/L
Urine
Blood 3+
Protein 1+
RBC 2–3/hpf
WBC 2–3/hpf
Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's anemia?"?

options.ope: Defective ankyrin in the RBC membrane

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with jaundice and back pain" -> "Elevated total bilirubin indicates possible hemolysis" -> "Low haptoglobin suggests hemolytic anemia" -> "Presence of hemoglobinuria indicates intravascular hemolysis" -> "Possible cause of hemolysis due to isoniazid use" -> "Isoniazid can induce oxidative stress" -> "Oxidative stress leads to hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency" -> "G6PD deficiency leads to absence of reduced glutathione" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has back pain and jaundice" -> "Laboratory findings show anemia and elevated bilirubin" -> "Low haptoglobin indicates hemolysis" -> "Intravascular hemolysis suggested by hemoglobinuria" -> "Isoniazid can cause oxidative damage" -> "Oxidative damage can lead to hemolysis" -> "Absence of reduced glutathione leads to increased oxidative stress" -> "Increased oxidative stress causes hemolysis" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with symptoms of jaundice and back pain" -> "Laboratory results show anemia and elevated bilirubin" -> "Low haptoglobin indicates hemolytic process" -> "Hemoglobinuria suggests intravascular hemolysis" -> "Isoniazid can cause oxidative stress" -> "Oxidative stress can lead to hemolysis" -> "Absence of reduced glutathione is a plausible cause" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has jaundice and back pain" -> "Anemia with elevated bilirubin suggests hemolysis" -> "Low haptoglobin indicates hemolytic anemia" -> "Hemoglobinuria suggests intravascular hemolysis" -> "Isoniazid can induce oxidative stress" -> "Oxidative stress can lead to hemolysis" -> "Absence of reduced glutathione may contribute to hemolysis" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings suggest hemolytic anemia, likely due to a condition such as G6PD deficiency, which is characterized by the absence of reduced glutathione leading to oxidative stress and hemolysis. The elevated indirect bilirubin and low haptoglobin support this diagnosis. The recent initiation of isoniazid, which can induce oxidative stress, may have precipitated the hemolysis in a patient with G6PD deficiency. Therefore, the most likely underlying cause of this patient's anemia is the absence of reduced glutathione.
